blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens at run time for `String result = "Hello" + " " + "World";`?

options.text: One StringBuilder is created, and the three parts are appended to it
options.says: The page says a + of compile-time constants is joined by the compiler, so no builder is made at run time.

options.text: Nothing is joined, as the compiler already made it one literal
options.says: The page says the compiler joins compile-time constants itself into the single literal "Hello World".

options.text: Two concat() calls are made, one for each of the + operators
options.says: The page says no concatenation happens at run time when every operand is a compile-time constant.

questions.stem: Per this page, since Java 9 what does `javac` emit for `greeting + " " + name`?

options.text: One invokedynamic call that StringConcatFactory links
options.says: The page says since Java 9 (JEP 280) javac emits one invokedynamic call to StringConcatFactory.

options.text: One new StringBuilder with three append calls on it
options.says: The page says that translation was javac's up to Java 8, not since Java 9.

options.text: One String.join call that takes all three operands
options.says: The page names invokedynamic and StringConcatFactory, not String.join, for this expression.

concepts: A + of compile-time constants is joined by the compiler into one literal, and no concatenation happens at run time.
Since Java 9, javac compiles + with variables into one invokedynamic call to StringConcatFactory.
